title: "03 Robust estimators under contamination"
author: "Saranjeet Singh Saluja"

How outliers bias robust estimators of center and scale, using the simulation study 2 data (contamination 0–20%).

- Figure S.11: sampling distributions of the median and MAD, Normal and Gamma
- Figure S.12: mean of each center and scale estimator by contamination level

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(arrow)
library(robustbase)
library(cowplot)

plot_dir <- "plots"
data_dir <- "data"

out_dir <- file.path(plot_dir, "thr3", "Miscellaneous")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Settings

The paper uses all 1,000 simulations. The estimates are saved to `est_file` and reused on later runs, so delete that file after changing `n_sims`.

```{r}
n_sims   <- 1000
pct_all  <- c("0%", "1%", "5%", "10%", "20%")
est_file <- file.path(data_dir, "robust_estimators_by_sim.parquet")
```

## Data

The raw file repeats each dataset for every iForest threshold; one copy is kept, since the estimators don't depend on it.

```{r}
df_results <- read_parquet(file.path(data_dir, "rawdata_simulations.parquet")) %>%
  filter(threshold == 0.6, simulation <= n_sims) %>%
  mutate(percentage = as.character(percentage))
```

## True values

True median and scaled MAD (1.4826 × MAD, equal to σ for a normal) of each uncontaminated distribution.
The MAD d solves F(m + d) − F(m − d) = 0.5, where m is the median.

```{r}
plaplace <- function(q, m = 0, b = 3) ifelse(q < m, 0.5 * exp((q - m) / b), 1 - 0.5 * exp(-(q - m) / b))

dist_info <- tribble(
  ~distribution, ~label,       ~true_median,
  "df_normal",   "Normal",     10,
  "df_T",        "T",          0,
  "df_laplace",  "Laplace",    0,
  "df_gamma",    "Gamma",      qgamma(0.5, 2, scale = 1),
  "df_chisq",    "Chi-square", qchisq(0.5, df = 3),
  "df_weibull",  "Weibull",    qweibull(0.5, shape = 1, scale = 3)
)

cdf_list <- list(
  df_normal  = function(q) pnorm(q, 10, 3),
  df_T       = function(q) pt(q, df = 4),
  df_laplace = function(q) plaplace(q),
  df_gamma   = function(q) pgamma(q, 2, scale = 1),
  df_chisq   = function(q) pchisq(q, df = 3),
  df_weibull = function(q) pweibull(q, shape = 1, scale = 3)
)

pop_scaled_mad <- function(cdf, m) {
  d <- uniroot(function(d) cdf(m + d) - cdf(m - d) - 0.5, c(1e-8, 100), tol = 1e-10)$root
  1.4826 * d
}

pop_ref <- dist_info %>%
  mutate(true_mad = map2_dbl(distribution, true_median, ~ pop_scaled_mad(cdf_list[[.x]], .y)))

dist_levels <- pop_ref$label
pop_ref
```

## Estimates

Median and Huber center; MAD, Sn, Qn and Huber scale (`MASS::hubers`, k = 1.5).
MAD, Sn and Qn use their normal-consistency constants. "0%" is each dataset's values before contamination.

```{r}
estimate_all <- function(x) {
  hub <- tryCatch(MASS::hubers(x), error = function(e) list(mu = NA_real_, s = NA_real_))
  tibble(Median      = median(x),
         HuberCenter = hub$mu,
         MAD         = mad(x),
         HuberScale  = hub$s,
         Sn          = Sn(x),
         Qn          = Qn(x))
}

if (file.exists(est_file)) {
  est_wide <- read_parquet(est_file)
} else {
  est_cont <- df_results %>%
    filter(percentage %in% pct_all) %>%
    group_by(distribution, percentage, simulation) %>%
    reframe(estimate_all(outlier_infused_values))

  # the original values are the same at every contamination level; take them from 1%
  est_orig <- df_results %>%
    filter(percentage == "1%") %>%
    group_by(distribution, simulation) %>%
    reframe(estimate_all(original_values)) %>%
    mutate(percentage = "0%")

  est_wide <- bind_rows(est_orig, est_cont)
  write_parquet(est_wide, est_file)
}

est_all <- est_wide %>%
  filter(percentage %in% pct_all) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Median, HuberCenter, MAD, HuberScale, Sn, Qn),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  left_join(pop_ref %>% dplyr::select(distribution, label), by = "distribution") %>%
  mutate(label      = factor(label, levels = dist_levels),
         percentage = factor(percentage, levels = pct_all),
         metric     = factor(metric, levels = c("Median", "HuberCenter", "MAD", "HuberScale", "Sn", "Qn")),
         group_type = if_else(metric %in% c("Median", "HuberCenter"), "Center", "Scale"))
```

## Figure S.12: mean estimates by contamination level

One panel per distribution; the dashed line is the true median (center) or true scaled MAD (scale).

```{r}
metric_colors <- c("Median" = "black",   "HuberCenter" = "#E31A1C",
                   "MAD"    = "black",   "HuberScale"  = "#E31A1C",
                   "Sn"     = "#377EB8", "Qn"          = "#E69F00")

line_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position    = "none",
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, color = "grey85"),
        strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
        strip.text.y.right = element_text(angle = 270),
        strip.placement    = "outside",
        axis.title         = element_text(size = 11),
        axis.text          = element_text(size = 9),
        panel.border       = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
        panel.spacing      = unit(0.8, "lines"))

plot_lines <- function(group, ref_col, ref_label) {
  sum_df <- est_all %>%
    filter(group_type == group) %>%
    group_by(label, percentage, metric) %>%
    summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  ref_df <- pop_ref %>%
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = dist_levels), true_value = .data[[ref_col]])

  ggplot(sum_df, aes(x = percentage, y = mean, color = metric, group = metric)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8, shape = 21, stroke = 0.35, color = "black") +
    geom_hline(data = ref_df, aes(yintercept = true_value, linetype = ref_label),
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", strip.position = "right") +
    scale_color_manual(values = metric_colors) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames("dashed", ref_label)) +
    labs(y = "Mean of estimates", x = "Outlier percentage", color = "Estimator", linetype = NULL) +
    line_theme
}
```

```{r, fig.height = 12, fig.width = 8}
p_center <- plot_lines("Center", "true_median", "True median")
p_scale  <- plot_lines("Scale",  "true_mad",    "True scaled MAD")

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "CenterEstimators-LineGraph_sans_30.png"), p_center, width = 5, height = 8)
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "ScaleEstimators-LineGraph_sans_30.png"),  p_scale,  width = 5, height = 8)

p_center
p_scale
```

Legends, saved separately and placed under each panel.

```{r}
leg_theme <- theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal",
                   legend.box = "horizontal", legend.text = element_text(size = 9))

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "Legend-Center-LineGraph.png"), ggdraw(get_legend(p_center + leg_theme)),
       width = 5, height = 0.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "Legend-Scale-LineGraph.png"), ggdraw(get_legend(p_scale + leg_theme)),
       width = 5, height = 0.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Figure S.11: sampling distributions of the median and MAD

One row per contamination level. The dark red line is the mean of the estimates and the black dashed line the true value.
The x-limits are fixed per distribution.

```{r}
hist_limits <- list(
  df_normal = list(Median = c(9.2, 10.6), MAD = c(2.5, 5.6)),
  df_gamma  = list(Median = c(1.3, 3.0),  MAD = c(0.8, 3.0))
)

plot_hist <- function(dist_key) {
  lims <- hist_limits[[dist_key]]
  d <- est_all %>%
    filter(distribution == dist_key, metric %in% c("Median", "MAD")) %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(as.character(metric), levels = c("Median", "MAD")))

  avg_df <- d %>%
    group_by(percentage, metric) %>%
    summarise(avg_value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  true_df <- d %>%
    distinct(percentage, metric) %>%
    mutate(true_value = if_else(metric == "Median",
                                pop_ref$true_median[pop_ref$distribution == dist_key],
                                pop_ref$true_mad[pop_ref$distribution == dist_key]))

  # invisible points that fix each column's x-range
  limits_df <- distinct(d, percentage) %>%
    crossing(tibble(metric = factor(c("Median", "Median", "MAD", "MAD"), levels = c("Median", "MAD")),
                    value  = c(lims$Median, lims$MAD)))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = value)) +
    geom_histogram(data = filter(d, metric == "Median"), aes(y = after_stat(density)),
                   binwidth = 0.05, boundary = lims$Median[1], closed = "left",
                   fill = "grey80", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_histogram(data = filter(d, metric == "MAD"), aes(y = after_stat(density)),
                   binwidth = 0.05, boundary = lims$MAD[1], closed = "left",
                   fill = "grey60", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_vline(data = avg_df,  aes(xintercept = avg_value),
               colour = "darkred", linewidth = 0.6, linetype = "solid") +
    geom_vline(data = true_df, aes(xintercept = true_value),
               colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_blank(data = limits_df, aes(x = value, y = 0)) +
    facet_grid(percentage ~ metric, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Density") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(panel.grid       = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
          strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
          axis.title       = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.text        = element_text(size = 8),
          panel.border     = element_rect(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25),
          panel.spacing    = unit(0.7, "lines"),
          legend.position  = "none")
}

for (dk in names(hist_limits)) {
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("Median_MAD_Histogram_", dk, "_sans_30.png")),
         plot_hist(dk), width = 6, height = 4 * length(pct_all) / 6)
}
```

## Bias relative to the true value

Mean estimate minus the true value, as a percentage of the true value, by distribution and contamination level.
For T and Laplace the true median is 0, so the center row is the raw difference × 100.

```{r}
est_all %>%
  left_join(pop_ref %>% dplyr::select(distribution, true_median, true_mad), by = "distribution") %>%
  mutate(true_value = if_else(group_type == "Center", true_median, true_mad)) %>%
  group_by(label, metric, percentage) %>%
  summarise(mean_est = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), true = first(true_value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(rel_bias_pct = round(100 * (mean_est - true) / abs(if_else(true == 0, 1, true)), 1)) %>%
  dplyr::select(label, metric, percentage, rel_bias_pct) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = percentage, values_from = rel_bias_pct)
```
